newsitem.title: UK: Copper, aluminium wake up to end around day's high.
newsitem.headline: Copper, aluminium wake up to end around day's high.

text.p: Late Tuesday LME trading saw copper and aluminium spring to life, with both markets probing higher in the final minutes of the kerb to end firm.
But the late uptick tended to disguise an otherwise drab day's trading, with volumes low-key and interest only patchy. Other metals were slow throughout the session, ttraders said.
"Copper was bought late because it was obvious that it was going to be a good chart close. Ally (aluminium) got through resistance and then set off short covering," one floor trader said.
The copper market spent most of the session just above $2,500, having recorded advances in early trade after a reasonable stock fall. The late jump took the the market to $2,514 a tonne, up $26.

More significantly, the backwardation widened throughout the session, and was around $85, basis cash/threes, by the close, against under $70 on Monday. July onwards is looking tight, some traders said.
Aluminium similarly saved its best till the end, with the market making a determined effort to wear down the resistance above $1,610, and last business was at $1,617, up $14 from Monday.

Traders said aluminium was boosted by LME warehouse and IPAI producer stock falls today, as well as signs that the contango may have started to contract again. June date pricing takes place next Monday, and the contango could narrow back in to around $15 again soon, from a current $20.

Nickel trading slowed during late afternoon, but prices remained steadier up to the kerb end. The market continues to watch for fresh developments at strikebound Inco, Sudbury, where the current stoppage could run into the annual summer holiday shut-downs, some traders said.
Prices subsided from above $7,300, but still finished at $7,290, a $40 gain from the previous kerb.

Zinc recovered some poise after Monday's correction to last week's run-up to 4-1/2 year highs, although the market is still some way off re-challenging its highs. Last trade was at $1,363, up $7 from yesterday.

Tin ran out of upside impetus in mid-afternoon, and settled back under liquidation to close at $5,590, up $10. The market was also affected by a widening in the contango, although upcoming tightness may not be diffused yet.
Lead business was featureless from the outset - hence little deviation from overnight levels. Prices closed at $640, against Monday's kerb close of $641.
Alloy was quiet, and three months was indicated at $1,470/80 a tonne, little different from Monday.
